desc: Read input N and S, and collect the 0-indexed positions of all '1's into a list.
Compute the transformed values $q_i = p_i - i$ for each '1' at position $p_i$ (where $i$ is the 0-based index in the list of 1s).

Find the median of the $q_i$ values. If $k$ is odd, it's the middle element; if even, any value between the two middle elements works, so we can pick either middle element (or check both, but typically one is sufficient for integer optimization).
Clamp the median value to the valid range $[0, N-k]$ to get the optimal starting position $s$.
Compute the total cost as $\sum |q_i - s|$ and print the result.
